note.explanation: A Boolean function takes one or more binary inputs and gives one binary output. Its inputs and output are only 0 or 1. AND, OR and NOT are used to build Boolean functions.
examples: For F(A, B) = A · B, the output is 1 only when A = 1 and B = 1.
For P = ¬A, if A = 1 then P = 0.
note.checkAnswer: For A = 1 and B = 0, A · B = 0 and A + B = 1.
note.simple: A Boolean function is a rule that takes in 0s and 1s and gives back a 0 or 1.

note.title: Boolean functions and basic logic
steps: Write the input values: A = 0 and B = 1.

written.text:
Consider a Boolean function with two inputs, A and B. We can construct a function F that represents the AND operation:
F ( A, B ) = A · B
written.finalAnswer: F(A, B) = A · B; the output is 1 only when A = 1 and B = 1.

rubric.why: The Boolean expression identifies the function being constructed.
rubric.how: Write F(A, B) = A · B.

rubric.why: The output condition shows the meaning of the AND function.

modelAnswer: F(A, B) = A · B
The output is 1 only when A = 1 and B = 1.

Now, let us construct a more complex Boolean function with three inputs, A, B, and C:

F (A, B, C) = A · B + A̅ · C

rubric.why: The intermediate columns apply the operations in the given expression.

rubric.how: Calculate (A · B) + (A̅ · C) for every row.

| A | B | C | A·B | A̅ | A̅·C | F(A, B, C) |
Final output values in row order: 0, 1, 0, 1, 0, 0, 1, 1.

written.finalAnswer: A truth table shows the output of a logic operation or Boolean function for all possible combinations of its inputs.

written.finalAnswer: A NOT gate gives the opposite of its input: A = 0 gives P = 1, and A = 1 gives P = 0.

written.text: Q3.1. Explain the usage of Boolean functions in computers.
written.finalAnswer: Boolean functions are used in computer ALUs for arithmetic operations, in memory and storage for data processing, and in control logic to coordinate system operations.

rubric.why: The textbook identifies arithmetic operations in ALUs as one computer use.
rubric.how: Mention that ALUs use Boolean functions for operations such as addition and subtraction.

rubric.why: Boolean functions also support the processing and handling of binary data.
rubric.how: Mention binary data processing in memory and storage.

rubric.why: Control logic is another distinct use of Boolean functions.
rubric.how: State that Boolean functions help coordinate system operations.

rubric.why: Examples from everyday devices support the explanation.
rubric.how: Mention a cell phone or calculator using Boolean logic to evaluate inputs and produce results.

modelAnswer: Boolean functions are used in Arithmetic Logic Units (ALUs) of CPUs to perform arithmetic operations such as addition, subtraction, multiplication and division.
They are used to process binary data in memory and storage devices, helping with data manipulation and retrieval.
They are used in control logic to coordinate different parts of a computer system's operation.
Cell phones and calculators also use Boolean functions to evaluate inputs and produce the required output.

explain.title: Binary variables
explain.body: Binary variables have only two possible values: 0 and 1. In logic, these may also be described as False and True.

explain.title: AND, OR and NOT
explain.body: AND gives 1 only when both inputs are 1. OR gives 1 when at least one input is 1. NOT takes one input and gives its opposite.

explain.title: Boolean functions
explain.body: A Boolean function is a function which has a one or more binary inputs and produces a single binary output. It is built using logic operations such as AND, OR and NOT.

explain.title: Truth tables and logic gates
explain.body: A truth table shows the output for every possible input combination. Logic gates are physical devices in electronic circuits that perform Boolean operations.

mistakes: Do not confuse AND and OR: AND needs both inputs to be 1, while OR needs at least one input to be 1.
Do not leave out an input combination when making a truth table.
For NOT, reverse the input: 0 becomes 1 and 1 becomes 0.
When evaluating a multi-part function, calculate each operation column before the final output column.
In Boolean logic, 1 + 1 for OR is 1, not 2.
